record.paper_title: Channel Training & Estimation for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces: Exposition of Principles, Approaches, and Open Problems
record.original_question: For RIS-aided sparse channel estimation in mmWave or THz settings, what pilot signals and RIS training states are optimal for sparse recovery, and what training-based capacity results follow when the channel is estimated through sparse recovery rather than standard linear estimation?

evidence.quote: A thorough characterization of optimal training with sparse recovery, and the associated training-based capacity (as in Sec. IV) is still open.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a narrowband MIMO communication link aided by a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS). Let the transmitter have $M_t$ antennas, the receiver have $M_r$ antennas, and the RIS have $N$ passive reflecting elements whose phase configuration at training slot $k$ is described by a diagonal matrix $\Theta_k = \mathrm{diag}(\theta_k) \in \mathbb{C}^{N\times N}$ with unit-modulus entries. Denote by $H_1 \in \mathbb{C}^{N\times M_t}$ the transmitter-to-RIS channel and by $H_2 \in \mathbb{C}^{M_r\times N}$ the RIS-to-receiver channel, so that the end-to-end (cascaded) channel for configuration $\Theta_k$ is
$$H(\Theta_k) \;=\; H_2\,\Theta_k\,H_1.$$
Assume a mmWave/THz propagation regime in which $H_1$ and $H_2$ admit sparse geometric representations
$$H_1 = A_R(\phi_1)\,\mathrm{diag}(\alpha_1)\,A_T(\psi_1)^H, \qquad H_2 = A_R(\phi_2)\,\mathrm{diag}(\alpha_2)\,A_T(\psi_2)^H,$$
where each link has only $L \ll \min(M_t,M_r,N)$ dominant paths with angles drawn from quantized dictionaries of sizes $G, H, P$ along the relevant spatial directions, and $\alpha_1,\alpha_2$ are complex gains. During training, the transmitter emits pilot symbols $\{x_k\}_{k=1}^{K}$ and the receiver observes
$$y_k = H_2\,\Theta_k\,H_1\,x_k + n_k, \qquad n_k \sim \mathcal{CN}(0,\sigma^2 I),$$
under an average pilot energy constraint $\sum_k \|x_k\|^2 \le K P_t$ and a total training budget of $K$ symbols (out of a coherence block of length $T$).

Within this model, address the following:

(a) Determine pilot signals $\{x_k\}_{k=1}^{K}$ and RIS training states $\{\Theta_k\}_{k=1}^{K}$ that are optimal (in a precise, stated sense such as minimizing worst-case or average mean-square error of the sparse-recovery estimate of $(H_1,H_2)$, or equivalently the cascaded channel, subject to the sparsity prior above) for recovery via $\ell_1$-minimization or other sparse-recovery decoders. The optimality criterion should account for the joint design of the pilot sequence and the RIS phase profiles, and should specify how restricted-isometry- or coherence-type guarantees are met with the minimum possible $K$.

(b) Derive a training-based capacity result for this RIS-aided channel in which the channel is acquired through the sparse-recovery estimator from part (a) rather than a standard linear (e.g., least-squares or LMMSE) estimator. Specifically, obtain a closed-form lower bound on the ergodic achievable rate of the form
$$R(K,P_t,T) = \frac{T-K}{T}\,\mathbb{E}\!\left[\log_2\det\!\left(I + \rho_{\mathrm{eff}}(K,P_t)\,\widehat H \widehat H^H\right)\right],$$
where $\widehat H$ is the sparse-recovery estimate and $\rho_{\mathrm{eff}}$ accounts for residual estimation error, and optimize this bound over $K$ to characterize the optimal training length and the resulting capacity scaling in $(M_t,M_r,N,L,T,P_t)$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and research papers on RIS-aided sparse channel estimation propose various compressive-sensing-based estimators (e.g., OMP-style algorithms with O(L log(P+GH)) pilot overhead) and pilot/RIS-phase designs, but none provide a complete characterization of jointly optimal pilots and RIS training states together with the corresponding training-based capacity. Overview papers from 2023–2024 explicitly identify this joint optimality and the associated capacity result as unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Channel Training & Estimation for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: A thorough characterization of optimal training with sparse recovery, and the associated training-based capacity is still open.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of jointly optimal training (pilots and RIS states) for sparse recovery and the corresponding training-based capacity is explicitly stated as open.

status_evidence.title: An Overview of Signal Processing Techniques for RIS/IRS-aided Wireless Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys recent sparse and compressive channel estimation methods for RIS, noting open issues in pilot/RIS-state design and overhead.
status_evidence.claim: Existing surveys list optimal pilot and RIS phase design for sparse recovery as an unresolved research direction.

status_evidence.title: Channel Estimation in RIS-Enabled mmWave Wireless Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Develops sparse-recovery algorithms for RIS mmWave channel estimation; focuses on MSE performance rather than full capacity characterization.
status_evidence.claim: Current sparse-recovery RIS estimators address MSE but do not give a complete training-based capacity characterization.
